correctness.rationale: Every unfolding has 16 unique length-four factors; any four marks are forced to 4,8,12,16 by disjoint coverage of four start positions per mark. The 16 binary de Bruijn cycles are exhaustively produced by two independent methods, all 256 cuts are directly checked against all distinct factors, and each non-four case has a verified five-position certificate. The finite proof does not infer an infinite theorem from experiments.

value.rationale: The 2024 literature explicitly asks whether suitable optimal cuts exist across de Bruijn cycles and how optimal sizes vary. At the first nonprime order for a binary alphabet, a complete natural 16-class census establishes optimal four-mark cut counts 8,12,16, proves every class has a good cut, and precisely characterizes the 64 exceptional cuts requiring five marks. This is a motivated finite complete classification, not a chosen-word anecdote or routine arithmetic substitution.
